title: Tokenizer-shared failures: do models with the same tokenizer family break on the same inputs?

original_idea.body:
# Tokenizer-shared failures

Assemble tokenization-stress inputs (long numbers, unusual unicode, glitch tokens); group open models by tokenizer lineage and test whether same-tokenizer models fail on the same inputs more than cross-tokenizer pairs. Inference only.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 3: plausible mechanistic chain but tokenization glitches map weakly to catastrophic risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 5: assemble stress inputs, group by tokenizer, measure failure overlap; standard tooling.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 4: focused deliverable with modest dependency on curating glitch inputs.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: open models with documented tokenizers, no internal access, weak lab incentive.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference only on a consumer GPU, light.

novelty.reasoning: Glitch tokens known; clustering correlated failure by tokenizer lineage is plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Tokenizer glitches documented; tokenizer-lineage as a homogeneity driver is plausibly open.
